title: Refuse forged landings of dispatched jobs that never closed
summary: Narrowed to one of the three forgeries in design §16.2 / acceptance-2: a landing forged for a job that was read and dispatched but never closed (a single hand-made commit adds the change and the closing records). The gate in athena-gate will refuse it. Goal: a maintainer running `athena check --history` or the commit-msg hook sees the forgery caught.

defaults_applied.how: Test replays the forgery; cargo test and clippy stay clean.
Criteria run the forged landing through the gate.
Check is the forged landing being refused, not the rule existing.
Rule is on the landing structure, not on one forged job.
Enforced in the gate, not prose.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: read crates/athena-gate/src/jobs.rs (entry `check`, which judges a job's records as a set, M27), listed crates/athena-gate/src/{history,records,landing_tests,reconcile,invariant}.rs and crates/athena-core/src/land.rs; the producer must read these for the order in which gate checks run. No new record or data file is added under crates/, so check_record_file/AnyRecord/round-trip tests are unaffected; if the producer adds one it must update them.

Chosen mechanism: structural, not cryptographic. A landing's closing records (outcome, score, usage, etc.) must follow a dispatched job's earlier records in history, and the gate refuses a single commit that adds the change together with all closing records for a job whose dispatch/verdict evidence is absent or was never closed by Athena. The producer may pick a different non-secret mechanism if the survey shows this one cannot work, and records the choice.

The other two forgeries (job fabricated record by record, hand-made proposal closed with `athena close`) remain open and are out of scope here as separate follow-up requests; signing or a key/witness ledger is also follow-up.
Only the gate and its tests change, plus the §16.2 and docs/enforcement.md text for this one route, and a CHANGELOG entry. Governance files (athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows) are not changed.
The new refusal is meant to hit only forged landings; genuine fake-agent jobs must still pass.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new test in crates/athena-gate (e.g. landing_tests.rs) builds a job that was read and dispatched but never closed, then a single commit adding the change plus four closing records, and asserts the gate returns a refusal for it. Run `cargo test -p athena-gate`.

A genuine fake-agent job still lands, closes, scores and passes the gate; all existing gate, CLI and core tests pass. Run `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`, all clean.

The change refuses more readings of history only for forged landings; replay of past readings expects 2% of newly refused readings, and the higher refusal rate is intended because forged landings must now fail.

docs/design/athena-v0.md §16.2 and docs/enforcement.md mark the forged-landing route as detected (Grep for it in both) and still state that the other two routes (fabricated job, hand-made proposal closed with athena close) pass; CHANGELOG.md records the change.
The refusal message names the job and says why, so a maintainer can tell a forged landing from a legitimate one; Grep the gate source for the message.

out_of_scope: Detecting a job fabricated record by record (follow-up request)
Detecting a hand-made proposal closed with athena close (follow-up request)
Keyed MAC, signing or a witness ledger outside the repo (follow-up request)
Changes to athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows or prompt files
departures: Scope cut to one forgery route so median wall time fits the verifier timeout; otherwise near the reference.
hard_reason: Adds a gate rule that can refuse landings, in the gate that judges other jobs and its history check.
